title: Arjahn
imageAlt: Portrait of Arjahn, a soldier, mapper, and protector
dek: Arjahn thinks beyond the first victory: routes, hazards, retreat, the next fight—and the relationships that must survive long enough to make any plan matter.

Gate chronicle · primary arrival and welcome scenes
body:
Arjahn’s planning is biography. He looks for environmental hazards, defensible routes, monster territory, and the path home after the battle everyone is currently discussing. He is interested not only in reaching a target, but in whether the party can survive what happens afterward.

The map as protection

When Wren develops a way to gather information from the landscape, Arjahn does not compete for ownership. He asks who will draw what she learns and offers magic to improve the work. His instinct is collaborative: a good solution belongs to the group and should be made more survivable.

Anger carried forward

After Olokun lashes out at him for risking another death, Arjahn names what the fear has erased: he has a wife and children, understands the cost, and is trying to keep Olokun alive too. Days later he offers a joke about weaponized paintbrushes because he does not want anger to become their last exchange.

Fear, then discipline

The broader record remembers a protector who can be terrified, physically overwhelmed, or furious without ceasing to act like a soldier. Courage is not calmness. It is regaining enough discipline to stand, plan, and protect the person beside him.

The western mist · fear as information

Arjahn’s unusual perception shows him something inside Babel-Ashur’s western mist that resembles every nightmare he has experienced at once. Outside the visible boundary he can still rationalize the sensation; his prediction of compounded fear and battle trauma inside is still a warning at that September stage. The October expedition below tests what entry can do.

He continues helping during the Spires’ reversed-gravity accident, then performs the group’s deliberate radiant test. His energy burns a temporary opening but produces a violently amplified reaction before the mist regenerates. The result unsettles him and teaches a new tactical limit: his own power can become more dangerous when the environment changes its scale.

October · the family he cannot leave behind

Arjahn proposes a tethered test of radiant protection. Wren ties his wrist and the others wait outside, ready to pull. Deeper in the fog, however, he sees a terrified young Sajhan calling him to save her mother. Convinced that his daughter needs him, he cuts the rope and runs. Scribonia becomes a pursuing monster in his perception; resistance meant to rescue him feels like another attack on his family.

The figure disappears and Arjahn is left lost, unable to move or speak. His thoughts return to his wife, son and daughter and to his conviction that he failed them. These are his experience and self-accusation inside the mist, not evidence that the family is physically present or that his guilt is an objective judgment.

Once the mist clears, he searches the sky for Sajhan before understanding what happened. He apologizes to Scribonia and says his protection failed with deeper or longer exposure, without knowing which caused it. He also admits he would run again if convinced his family were real. His planning has encountered a vulnerability he can name without promising it is cured.

October · refusing a world chosen by one will

Death’s offer comes while Arjahn is still furious. He strikes the figure with lightning, then accuses him of killing his family and harming civilians. The accusations remain Arjahn’s account; the encounter does not newly reconstruct each death.

After receiving a vision, Arjahn still refuses trust: suffering does not excuse the harm done to others. He challenges destruction as a substitute for healing, even while recognizing his own wish to destroy Babel-Ashur. When Death leaves the choice to him, he answers that no single being should decide for everyone, even if that being chose correctly. His rejection includes scrutiny of his own anger.

He ends the surviving scene with a quieter duty: escorting Nymera and the exhausted Scribonia toward the cave, prepared to provide healing when they arrive.

The Vanguard · May 2026

During the Babel-Ashur crisis, Arjahn was reported to be part of a vanguard that was losing. This early Vanguard reference is supplemented by Mya’s account of a scattered first wave and Nuru preparing a more focused second force; formal ranks and membership remain unresolved. It extends Arjahn’s history into an active front under severe pressure, but it does not identify his rank, mission, comrades, or eventual fate.

Learning to address the survivor

At Skylight Refuge, Arjahn asks another survivor about the mind of the freed captive before speaking to Kyrin himself. He recognizes the mistake and apologizes. He distinguishes healing an arm from repairing a mind or soul, and offers help without promising a magical cure. When Kyrin blames his people for losing the land, Arjahn insists that being attacked was not their fault.

August · protecting civilians and refusing another loss

Arjahn stays to defend Skylight Refuge with Eugene and Nymera. He rejects fighting among the civilians if a position outside can draw danger away. During the battle he says their own lives must come second to the refugees, then struggles with what that judgment would mean for the wounded Nymera beside him.

After Eugene’s Wish destroys the attackers and Nymera falls dead with them, Arjahn reaches her and casts Revivify. The narrator explicitly records her return and says the diamond is not consumed in this case. Through tears, he calls her Sajhan before recognizing the name he has used. This reveals his own grief; it does not identify Nymera as his daughter.

His apology to Nymera follows the return: he says he did not mean that he could abandon her. Later, exhausted and unfit for the renewed fight, he withdraws. Her second death happens after that withdrawal. The record does not turn either his earlier resolve or his retreat into proof that he could have controlled every outcome.

Vengeance and the mountain

Before the mountain assault, Arjahn admits that his immediate desire is vengeance rather than rebuilding. He understands that collapsing the stronghold could endanger hidden people, yet argues that the offensive must proceed. He redirects water, casts an earthquake on the mountainside and carries Eugene out of the flood. His continued care for companions coexists with this darker turn; one does not erase the other. The account posted on 29 August 2026 (UTC) leaves the full aftermath unresolved.

The later October mist expedition establishes that Abyss remains active after this assault. That discovery does not change what the company could know through the storm and smoke at the time.

Offering Animak a first foothold

At the Gate, Arjahn checks Animak for injury, offers shelter and service in Pristinia, and is startled when the newcomer disappears into a lantern. He listens until Animak finds a way out, then returns it. On the road he explains that his own way of fighting Death is keeping others alive, while admitting he does not know how the wider struggle will end. He also speaks of his lost wife and children; Animak’s apology meets reassurance rather than blame. Read Animak’s arrival.

Babel · the supply run that becomes a loss

The first hunts show Arjahn spending magic to help companions move through the jungle, then treating injuries that leave less power for the next fight. In February, after Aravil’s capture, he wants something on which to spend his anger. Aerrow pushes him back toward their practical purpose: supplies and a safer place to return.

He declines to pursue a passing monster because he will not risk Aerrow for his own recklessness. The later encounter still overwhelms them. Arjahn revives Aerrow once, loses him again and escapes with the body. At the Refuge he blames himself for holding back his only powerful diamond. Elenia later raises Aerrow, without an identified spell in this passage. The record preserves Arjahn’s choices and regret without making his self-condemnation an omniscient verdict.

By June, supply gathering also means protecting rescued civilians. He calls for a rear guard, tells Gartina to leave her materials safe at camp and argues that conversation outside must give way to caution. Scribonia defends the value of social bonds. The subsequent dragon fight does not independently prove either man’s account of what caused the danger.

Scenes in sequence

Selected scenes follow choices, knowledge and consequences. Dates identify UTC source postings; this October session was played on 18 October in New York.

  1. 2026-02-06 · quest

    Anger meets the responsibility for a companion

    Arjahn agrees not to seek revenge at Aerrow’s expense, then loses him in a later encounter despite a temporary Revivify.

    Known at this stage
    He wants a fight but knows another person shares the risk.
    Consequence
    The retreat becomes a lasting source of guilt.
    Still unresolved
    His regret does not establish that he controlled every outcome.

  2. 2026-06-23 · quest

    A supply run exposes different needs

    Arjahn demands silence while Scribonia argues for rebuilding social bonds; Gartina tries to redirect the conversation.

    Known at this stage
    The group is gathering resources for a shelter shared with survivors.
    Consequence
    Practical care and strained relationships have to coexist.
    Still unresolved
    The later encounter does not prove that conversation caused the dragon’s attack.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6 · Receipt 7

  3. 2026-08-19 · quest

    Revivify and an apology

    Arjahn restores Nymera with Revivify after the first defense and apologizes for speaking as if he could abandon her.

    Known at this stage
    He has put civilian safety first while still trying to keep companions alive.
    Consequence
    Personal attachment challenges his earlier language of expendable soldiers.
    Still unresolved
    The unconsumed diamond is a narrated exception here; calling Nymera Sajhan does not identify her as his daughter.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6

  4. 2026-10-19 · quest

    A tether cannot withstand a believable family emergency

    Arjahn cuts his safety rope and pursues an apparent Sajhan, then becomes lost and paralyzed.

    Known at this stage
    He believes his family needs rescue and perceives Scribonia as a monster.
    Consequence
    The earlier warning about fear becomes a directly observed danger of entry.
    Still unresolved
    The vision establishes neither a living Sajhan at this location nor the objective truth of Arjahn’s self-blame.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6 · Receipt 7 · Receipt 8

  5. 2026-10-19 · quest

    Refusal followed by an escort home

    Arjahn rejects Death’s offer after the vision and escorts the companions who are carrying Scribonia back.

    Known at this stage
    His fury includes a desire to destroy the island; he recognizes the tension with his argument for healing.
    Consequence
    The refusal leads back to immediate care rather than ending at a declaration.
    Still unresolved
    Neither the shared vision’s contents nor every claim about the family’s deaths is independently established here.

brief.status: Alive after the October mist expedition; escorts Nymera and the exhausted Scribonia toward the refuge (19 October 2026 UTC source posts).
brief.basis: Existing public dossier, explicit status facts and named timeline participants. Selected events are a reading guide, not a complete list or a ranking of importance.

profile.personality: Arjahn thinks like a soldier responsible for bringing people home. He can become sharp when fear or loss overwhelms a plan, but he values routes, maps, accountability, and the difficult work of repairing trust after people have said what pressure made them say.
profile.achievements: He helps expose the false distress call in The Before, survives the cave collapse and contamination crisis, resurrects Olokun with the Scepter of Faith, and later burns a temporary opening in Babel-Ashur’s western mist. His best deeds combine force with preparation: escape routes, shared maps, and evidence that others can use.
profile.relationships: His bond with Olokun survives anger, near-death, and reconciliation through work. Wren, Dale, Vaemyr, Gudlaug, Tricks, and Leo appear across his field history, while his later service with the Vanguard places him inside a larger responsibility to people who may never know the individual choices that kept them alive.

sourceReview.scope: Selected Mark of the Wild character/narrator prose and targeted combat outcomes, with the later primary Babel return scene. No exhaustive mechanics/attachment audit or private revelation import.
